title: Classic Butter Shortbread
subtitle: slice-and-bake butter rounds with a sugar-sparkle edge that melt in your mouth
imageAlt: Round pale-golden butter shortbread cookies fanned on a white plate on a navy napkin
servingsNote: about 30 cookies: 3 each, and a tin to give away

beforeYouStart.text: The butter must be soft: it should dent easily but not look greasy. Leave it out about an hour.
The logs chill 30 minutes before slicing (included in the time), or keep in the fridge up to 3 days.

steps.title: Cream
steps.text: Beat the soft butter, icing sugar, vanilla and salt with an electric mixer about 2 minutes, until pale and creamy.

steps.title: Add the flour
steps.text: Mix in the flour on low just until it comes together into a soft dough. Don't overmix.

steps.title: Shape and chill
steps.text: Divide in half and roll each into a log about 4 cm across. Roll the logs in the sugar, wrap and chill 30 minutes, until firm.

steps.title: Slice
steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C (325°F) and line 2 baking sheets with parchment. Slice the logs 1 cm thick and set the rounds 2 cm apart.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake both sheets 18–20 minutes, swapping racks halfway, until the bottoms are lightly golden and the tops still pale. Cool 5 minutes on the sheets, then move to a rack.

fixIt.fix: Knead it a few times with your hands; their warmth brings it together.
The butter was too soft or the logs too warm. Chill the sliced rounds 10 minutes before baking.
Shortbread should stay pale. If your oven runs hot, bake at 150°C (300°F) a few minutes longer.
Let them sit out 5 minutes and use a thin, sharp knife.

saleTip: Butter is the main cost here. No Frills butter sales in December often hit $4.99–5.49 a pound, and it freezes for months.
swap: Pressed shortbread: pat the dough into a 20 cm (8-inch) square pan, prick all over with a fork and bake 30–35 minutes at 160°C (325°F); cut into fingers while warm.
leftovers: Crumble over berries and whipped cream for a quick trifle.
doneness: Bottoms lightly golden and tops pale. They're soft out of the oven and turn crisp and tender as they cool.
source: Based on classic Scottish-Canadian shortbread ratios (Canadian Living, Robin Hood): about 1 part sugar, 2 parts butter, 3 parts flour by weight, baked low and slow.
prepAhead: Keep the wrapped logs in the fridge up to 3 days, or freeze up to 3 months and slice from almost-frozen.
reheat: Not needed. Serve at room temperature.

basic.note: Just butter, sugar, flour and salt: no vanilla, no sugar coating.

stepNotes.2: Basic: skip the sugar coating; just wrap and chill.

fancy.note: Half-dipped in chocolate with festive sprinkles.

addSteps.title: Chocolate dip
addSteps.text: Melt the chocolate in a heatproof bowl in the microwave in 20-second bursts, stirring between, until smooth. Dip half of each cooled cookie, set on parchment, add sprinkles and let set 30 minutes (or 10 in the fridge).

plating: Stack them chocolate-side out in a short tower.
Tie a tin with ribbon to give away.

why.0-1: Icing sugar dissolves completely, which is what gives shortbread its melt-away texture.
why.0-4: Mixing just until combined keeps them tender, not tough.

funFact: Shortbread came to Canada with Scottish settlers. “Short” is an old baker's word for crumbly: all that butter coats the flour and keeps the dough from turning chewy.

keeps.note: the baked cookies or the wrapped raw logs
keeps.thaw: Cookies: on the counter about 1 hour. Raw logs: in the fridge overnight, then slice and bake
